question: The sides of a triangle are 90 cm, 11 cm and 97 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with the length of 11 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sides = 90, 11, 97

s = (90 + 11 + 97)/2 = 99

Area = √[99×9×88×2] = √156816 = 396

Altitude = (2×Area)/base = (2×396)/11

**∴ Answer = 72 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides = 90 cm, 11 cm, 97 cm

**Formula used:**

Heron’s formula: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]

Altitude = (2 × Area) / base

**Calculation:**

⇒ s = (90 + 11 + 97)/2 = 99

⇒ Area = √[99(99−90)(99−11)(99−97)]

⇒ = √[99 × 9 × 88 × 2]

⇒ = √156816 = 396

⇒ Altitude on side 11 = (2 × 396) / 11

⇒ = 792 / 11 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron’s Formula

Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]

Altitude Formula

Height = (2 × Area) / base

Triangle Check

Sum of any two sides must be greater than third
